construct: Activated CD4+ T cells express CD40 ligand (CD154), which binds CD40 on B cells and provides an essential signal for germinal-center responses and immunoglobulin class switching. Loss of CD40L prevents effective switching from IgM to IgG, IgA, and IgE and also impairs other CD40-dependent immune functions, predisposing to recurrent pyogenic and opportunistic infections.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The infection pattern plus low IgG/IgA, normal-to-high IgM, and preserved B-cell numbers identifies a T-cell help defect in immunoglobulin class switching, specifically CD40L deficiency.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: B7-CD28 costimulation is essential for naive T-cell activation and is the strongest alternative immune-pair distractor, but it does not directly provide the B-cell class-switch signal producing hyper-IgM.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only CD40L on activated CD4+ T cells engaging CD40 on B cells directly explains preserved B-cell numbers with failure to switch from IgM to downstream isotypes.
